newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian troops kill five militants in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Indian troops kill five militants in Kashmir.

text.p: Indian paramilitary forces shot dead five separatist guerrillas in a gunbattle on Thursday in troubled Jammu and Kashmir state, an Indian defence spokesman said.

"Soldiers, on a specific information, laid siege to a village in Sumbal and asked hiding militants to surrender. The militants opened fire and five of them, including three foreign mercenaries, were killed in the exchange," the spokesman said.
Sumbal is a small town 25 km (15 mile) north of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
Three houses caught fire and were gutted during the fighting, he said.
In a separate incident on Wednesday evening, five separatist guerrillas were killed in a shoot-out in the Rajouri district of Jammu region, a police spokesman said.
Rajouri lies near the India-Pakistan border about 250 km (150 mile) south of Srinagar.
"All five were foreign mercenaries," the spokesman said.
India controls two-thirds of Kashmir and Pakistan the rest.
More than a dozen guerrilla groups have fought a rebellion in Indian-administered Kashmir since 1990. Some demand an independent homeland while others want a merger with Pakistan.
Indian authorities say Pakistan trains and arms mercenaries and Kashmiri militants. Islamabad denies the charges and says it offers only political and diplomatic support.
More than 20,000 people have been killed in a seven-year-old rebellion in the Himalayan region.
